title: Python module batch A: input/output, variables, types, arithmetic (4 lessons + exercises)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). This batch delivers the first four lessons of the Python beginner module, covering the foundational input/output model, variables, core types, and arithmetic. Each lesson must be schema-valid, correctness-verified, and pass technical + pedagogy review. These lessons are the building blocks all subsequent Python lessons depend on.
objective: Author four Python beginner lessons covering input/output, variables, basic types (int/float/str/bool), and arithmetic operations — each with original prose, at least one runnable example, at least one graded exercise (solutionVerified:true, starter fails), and passing technical + pedagogy review.
acceptanceCriteria: Four lessons are delivered: (1) input and output with print() and input(), (2) variables and assignment, (3) core types (int, float, str, bool) and type(), (4) arithmetic operators and operator precedence.
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with a reference solution (solutionVerified:true by CI) and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson (Python official docs preferred); no copied or paraphrase-laundered prose.
Each lesson is schema-valid against the lesson and exercise JSON Schemas.
Technical correctness is reviewed for each lesson by a reviewer who is not the author.
Pedagogy checklist is signed off for each lesson by a reviewer who is not the author.
Examples are neutral/inclusive; prerequisites are honestly stated; single clear objective per lesson.
output: Four merged lesson documents (with associated exercise files) for input/output, variables, types, and arithmetic in Python, each schema-valid, correctness-verified, and reviewed.
